superseded_versions: classic-lr-v4 (trained, never released -- see notes below)
changes: Relabeled the annotation backlog (positive-example messages roughly doubled since the previous training round) and rebuilt the frozen train/val/test split from the updated data.

Permanently froze the test set to the same 754 message ids used by the previous release's split, so this and future model generations are compared on identical held-out data instead of a freshly re-cut test set each round.

Found and fixed a real train/val/test leakage bug in the split logic: near-duplicate reposted content (the same copy-pasted news story or marketing template reappearing under a different message id) was landing on both sides of the split under the old exact-byte-match dedup. Added near-duplicate clustering (normalized text + rare-word inverted index + similarity confirmation, gated on candidate-code compatibility so same-template-different-company posts aren't wrongly merged) so whole duplicate clusters are assigned to one split.

Found and fixed a privacy/feature-quality bug during the pre-release check: the word-level TF-IDF vectorizer used scikit-learn's default token pattern, which does not segment Chinese text -- an entire unspaced Chinese sentence was tokenized as a single 'word', so the vocabulary contained near-verbatim fragments of scraped training text. Fixed by restricting the word tokenizer to ASCII words or single CJK characters, leaving Chinese generalization to the (already fine-grained, unaffected) character n-gram vectorizer. Retrained classic-lr-v4 into classic-lr-v5 with this fix; v4 was never released.

pre_release_checks.split_leakage_audit: passed after fix -- normalized-text + rare-word-index + SequenceMatcher scan found zero remaining cross-split near-duplicates above the similarity threshold that weren't legitimate same-template-different-entity content
pre_release_checks.privacy_audit: passed after fix -- scanned word_vectorizer.vocabulary_ for entries >15 chars; the whole-sentence leak class is eliminated; residual long entries are wallet-address-like strings and adjacent-handle bigrams, which are expected/unavoidable content for a bag-of-words model trained on public social media text, not a structural leak
pre_release_checks.serving_smoke_test: passed -- scored synthetic messages through SemanticMatcher.score() (the same code path ws_client.py calls), including a known false-positive collision case ("NOW" as an emphatic adverb), which was correctly rejected
pre_release_checks.latency_test: passed -- multi-candidate p99 well under the 100ms budget
pre_release_checks.rollback_drill: passed -- the previous production model (archived separately) was loaded and scored standalone through the same serving code path to confirm a rollback is a simple file-swap

known_limitations: classic-lr-v5 precision (0.938) is below the project's 98% long-term target; the project decided 98% is an ongoing optimization goal, not a release gate for v0.1.0
candidate recall itself is capped around 97.5% upstream of this classifier (rule-layer recall), independent of this fix

word-vectorizer vocabulary still contains short tokens drawn from public social-media text (usernames, wallet-address-like strings) -- inherent to any bag-of-words model trained on real text, disclosed in the model card rather than treated as a fixable bug
